images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of Belief-Trajectory Energy (BTE).BTE quantifies the layerwise predictive revisions induced by an input and aggregates them into a depth profile. The profile can be further summarized into a scalar for training-free data difficulty measurement, and used directly to distinguish human-LLM reviews and attribute responses to generators.
Figure 2:Response-disruption control.Layer-wise BTE change relative to normal responses.

Solid: reference solution scored given its problem, five scorers ordered red→\toteal by strength; dashed: problem statement only (Llama). Bars: 95% bootstrap CI (Llama).
Figure 4:Depth profiles of generated reviews relative to human reviews of the same papers, per layer, under the Llama-3.1-8B (left) and Qwen-3.5-9B (right) scorers.

Figure 6:Familiarity and the depth profile.A: OLMo-2-7B stage-1 checkpoints from 0.5T to the 4T final model.B: mean profile before and after fine-tuning on 1k, 5k and 9.7k MATH solutions; shading gives the GSM8K drop at each dose and the dashed line the MATH-500 drop (right axis).C: relative change per layer for the three training arms, with the GSM8K drop per arm shaded and the MATH-500 drop dashed as in A. Figure 8:Attribution features. Each layer column of the token×\timeslayer BTE matrix (left)
is summarised over tokens (middle) and the resulting per-layer statistics are concatenated
into 32D-352D feature vectors (right).

Figure 9:Held-out reviews of the eight sources under the Llama scorer, for the four feature sets of Table2. Each panel is a nonlinear (t-SNE) map of the reviews’ scores on the seven LDA discriminant axes fitted on calibration papers; contours enclose 90% and 50% of each source’s estimated density, dots mark centroids. Map distances are not calibrated: only cluster overlap is meaningful. Richer token statistics separate Human and the three legacy generators from the newer ones; GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 remain overlapped and account for most residual errors.
